    Strings and string modules (Definitions 3.4–3.6, Construction 3.5) #

    A letter is an arrow with a direction (true for a direct letter a, false for a formal inverse a⁻¹). A word is a start vertex and a composable list of letters. Its string diagram has positions 0, …, n; letter i (0-based) joins positions i and i + 1, and the arrow acts from i to i + 1 for a direct letter and from i + 1 to i for an inverse letter.

    The coefficient quiver of a word (Word.coeffQuiver) records these arrow actions with coefficient one. A word is a string (Word.IsString) when no position has two outgoing or two incoming edges with the same label (no adjacent a a⁻¹ or a⁻¹ a) and no directed walk of its diagram spells a zero path. For monomial data this is Definition 3.4, phrased on the string diagram (Definition 3.6): a directed walk in a diagram without such forks runs along a direct or inverse subword. The string module (Word.stringModule) is the module of Construction 3.5.
